works.title: Friendship, Wisconsin
works.description: A contemporary American novel exploring rural economic decline, political betrayal, and personal redemption. Structured as first-person framing with third-person flashbacks, following a man's return to his economically hollowed hometown to reconnect with his attorney brother, who serves as witness to systemic collapse through job losses, factory closures, political disillusionment, and broken institutions. Thematically aligned with Steinbeck's critique of economic extraction.
works.quote: **Title: Friendship, Wisconsin** **Narrative Framework** - **Structure**: First-person framing from the narrator returning to his hometown for the summer, interwoven with third-person flashbacks based on stories told by his brother, old friends, and townsfolk.
